SharedFlowBundle.name: ISAM-Common-ExtractClientCert
SharedFlowBundle.Description:
Reusable building block: resolves the caller's client certificate into canonical variables, so every SAML/JWT type embeds the same values in its request to ISAM instead of each type reading a header directly.
OUTPUT variables: client.cert.base64 string, the client's X.509 certificate as BARE base64 -- no "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----"/"-----END CERTIFICATE-----" armor, no internal line-wrap whitespace, exactly the form ISAM's request expects. Null if the caller presented no certificate through either source below. client.cert.subject.dn string, the cert's subject Distinguished Name, plain text. client.cert.issuer.dn string, the cert's issuer Distinguished Name, plain text. client.cert.subject.dn.base64 the same subject DN, base64-encoded (this, not the plain-text form above, is what goes in the request to ISAM). client.cert.issuer.dn.base64 the same issuer DN, base64-encoded.
The four DN variables are only populated via source 1 below (tls.client.s.dn / tls.client.i.dn) -- the header fallback never carries a pre-parsed DN, only the raw cert, so all four stay null whenever client.cert.base64 was resolved from request.header.X-Client-Cert instead.
Two sources, tried in order: 1. tls.client.raw.cert (PEM) / tls.client.s.dn / tls.client.i.dn -- what Apigee itself captured during a two-way TLS handshake on its own VirtualHost. This is the authoritative source when mutual TLS terminates AT Apigee. These are ONLY populated if the VirtualHost is configured for client auth: - Edge Private/Public Cloud: the VirtualHost's SSLInfo needs ClientAuthEnabled set to true, plus a TrustStore holding the accepted client CA chain. - Apigee X/hybrid: the environment's TLS config has propagateTLSInformation.clientProperties = true. That configuration lives on the VirtualHost/environment, not in any proxy or shared flow bundle, so it will not show up in this repo -- if client.cert.base64 keeps coming back null in an environment where you expect mTLS at the gateway, check that config first, not this bundle's policies. tls.client.raw.cert comes back PEM-armored (with BEGIN/END lines and line-wrap whitespace); stripping that down to the bare base64 stored in client.cert.base64 takes 4 chained policy STEPS (AM-Extract-Client-Cert-TLS, then -Strip-Step2, -Strip-Step3, -Strip-Final, each writing one intermediate client.cert.base64.stepN variable the next one reads), not 4 AssignVariable blocks inside one policy: on a real trace, a later block reading a variable an EARLIER block in that SAME policy had just set came back unresolved, while a later STEP reading a variable a PRIOR STEP had set worked reliably. If you ever need to chain a transformation like this yourself, split it across policy steps, not AssignVariable blocks, until/unless you've independently confirmed same-policy chaining works on your specific Apigee version. 2. request.header.X-Client-Cert -- a certificate forwarded by an upstream device (a load balancer or reverse proxy in front of Apigee) that terminates mutual TLS itself, expected already in bare base64 (no PEM armor, no URL-encoding). Only used as a fallback when tls.client.raw.cert is unset, i.e. Apigee did not itself terminate mTLS for this request.
Every type-specific shared flow (ISAM-SAML-Light, ISAM-SAML-User, ISAM-SAML-TP, ISAM-SAML-Technical, ISAM-JWT-SAML, ISAM-JWT-Token) calls this one via FlowCallout early in its flow, before building its request to ISAM, and reads these variables afterwards.
